{
  "summary": "In `net_processing`, ignore `MSG_WITNESS_TX` entries in `INV` messages on `wtxidrelay` connections and consolidate the per-message deduplication sets into one. Move the tx-announcement protocol violation check before the announcement-type filtering so sending any transaction `INV` on a connection where transaction relay is disabled triggers a disconnect. Extend functional tests to verify block-relay-only connections disconnect on all tx `INV` variants.",
  "problem": "BIP 144 specifies that `MSG_WITNESS_TX` is only valid for `getdata` messages, but Bitcoin Core continued treating it as a valid announcement by txid on `wtxidrelay` connections. Additionally, peers on connections with tx relay disabled (such as block-relay-only connections) were not disconnected for sending tx announcements if those announcements used the wrong inv type for the connection, because type-mismatch checks were evaluated before the disconnect check.",
  "evidence": [
    "Commit 2eefc296d4 notes that 'BIP 144 specifies that MSG_WITNESS_TX is \"only for use in getdata\", so if we receive it anyway, ignore it, rather than treating it as a by-txid announcement.'",
    "PR description points out that attempting to announce transactions on `fRelay=false` was not triggering disconnects if the peer used an unexpected inv type due to check ordering."

result.summary: In `net_processing`, ignore `MSG_WITNESS_TX` entries in `INV` messages on `wtxidrelay` connections and consolidate the per-message deduplication sets into one. Move the tx-announcement protocol violation check before the announcement-type filtering so sending any transaction `INV` on a connection where transaction relay is disabled triggers a disconnect. Extend functional tests to verify block-relay-only connections disconnect on all tx `INV` variants.
result.problem: BIP 144 specifies that `MSG_WITNESS_TX` is only valid for `getdata` messages, but Bitcoin Core continued treating it as a valid announcement by txid on `wtxidrelay` connections. Additionally, peers on connections with tx relay disabled (such as block-relay-only connections) were not disconnected for sending tx announcements if those announcements used the wrong inv type for the connection, because type-mismatch checks were evaluated before the disconnect check.
evidence: Commit 2eefc296d4 notes that 'BIP 144 specifies that MSG_WITNESS_TX is "only for use in getdata", so if we receive it anyway, ignore it, rather than treating it as a by-txid announcement.'
PR description points out that attempting to announce transactions on `fRelay=false` was not triggering disconnects if the peer used an unexpected inv type due to check ordering.
result.card: Ignores invalid MSG_WITNESS_TX announcements in INV messages on wtxidrelay connections and ensures any tx INV received on a block-relay-only connection disconnects the peer. Previously, BIP 144 protocol violations could be treated as valid txid announcements, and sending misformatted tx INVs bypassed disconnection on connections where tx relay was disabled. The PR also simplifies net_processing by deduplicating INV hashes in a single set.
